summary: Charleston County, SC 60-foot steel tower on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway, built around the 1940s and removed in the 1960s; registered 2011.

facts.status_note: The register says the tower was removed in the 1960s

events.note: Registered April 7, 2011; nominated by Ron Stafford

evidence.supports: built around the 1940s; 60-foot steel tower on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway; removed in the 1960s
evidence.quote: Built circa the 1940s, this 60' steel tower located on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway was removed in the 1960s.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service
Forest Lookouts places the site in Charleston County under Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge
evidence.quote: Charleston County - Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge

evidence.supports: the refuge is governed by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
evidence.quote: Governing body U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the FFLOS register (1) gives the build date, height, location and removal, and the Forest Lookouts South Carolina index (2) gives only the county and refuge. The 1940s and 1960s dates are the register's own approximations. Registry number US 917, SC 3. Horsehead Lookout (NHLR) is a similar 60-foot steel tower on the Intracoastal Waterway but a different site; it was seen only in a search snippet and is not used. A Fish and Wildlife Service photo titled 'Fire tower' (fws.gov/media/fire-tower) is not labelled with a tower name and was not used. No staffing, fire or access information found, so those are left out. Two WebSearch queries were used.
